step 21: allow 22/tcp

  run:
    $ ufw allow 22/tcp comment 'paisans-f2a9: ssh, the bootstrap route'

step 22: allow 51820/udp
  firewall: allow 51820/udp (WireGuard, the mesh)
  run:
    $ ufw allow 51820/udp comment 'paisans-f2a9: WireGuard, the mesh'

step 23: allow all inbound on psns-f2a9
  firewall: allow all inbound on psns-f2a9 (the mesh: etcd, Patroni, Garage, HAProxy)
  run:
    $ ufw allow in on psns-f2a9 comment 'paisans-f2a9: the mesh: etcd, Patroni, Garage, HAProxy'

step 24: allow routed from psns-f2a9 back out psns-f2a9
  firewall: allow routed from psns-f2a9 back out psns-f2a9 (the mesh, relayed between sites that cannot dial each other)
  run:
    $ ufw route allow in on psns-f2a9 out on psns-f2a9 comment 'paisans-f2a9: the mesh, relayed between sites that cannot dial each other'

step 25: allow 80/tcp

  run:
    $ ufw allow 80/tcp comment 'paisans-f2a9: public ports, HTTP'

step 26: allow 443/tcp

step 27: allow 443/udp

warning: delegation reaches paisans-f2a9's manager at its next start
  Its manager is running, and restarting it would restart its Docker daemon and every container in it, so admit does not. cpuset and io limits apply after the host's next reboot.
warning: watchdog: falling back to softdog
  the watchdog will be softdog. It reboots the host when Patroni hangs, but not when the kernel does, and a hung kernel cannot fence itself any other way. A hardware or hypervisor watchdog is better: enable one in the firmware or the VM's settings, and admit again.
warning: watchdog: paisans-f2a9's Patroni can reboot this machine
  Patroni arms the watchdog and reboots the whole host when it stops renewing it, which is what makes its failover safe.
warning: public ports: every local user on this host may bind ports 80 to 1023
  net.ipv4.ip_unprivileged_port_start = 80 is host wide: no user's process needs root for a port from 80 up, the deployment's Caddy among them.
warning: forwarding: this turns on routing between every interface on this host
  Other sites dial this one, so it relays mesh traffic between sites behind NAT, which cannot dial each other. The firewall's route rule relays the mesh, and its forward policy governs every other route.
